Feature decoding model: predict a feature space from activity patterns

Source: R/feature_decode_model.R
feature_decode_model.Rd

The pattern-level complement of [banded_ridge_model()]. Within each region or searchlight, the feature columns of a [feature_sets_design()] are predicted from the local activity pattern by cross-validated ridge regression, and the held-out predictions are summarised over the declared structure of the feature space: every set, every family of sets, and every contrast (see [feature_sets()]). Family and contrast summaries are computed from the same held-out predictions, so they need no additional fits.

Usage

feature_decode_model(
  dataset,
  design,
  outer_crossval = NULL,
  tune_crossval = NULL,
  alphas = 10^seq(-1, 5),
  purge = 0L,
  nuisance = NULL,
  nuisance_fit = c("train", "within"),
  partial = FALSE,
  n_perm = 0L,
  perm_strategy = c("circular_shift", "block_shuffle"),
  perm_block = NULL,
  min_shift = 1L,
  min_voxels = 2L,
  seed = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

dataset

An `mvpa_dataset`; rows of its training data are the observations (for example volumes of one run).

design

A [feature_sets_design()] whose training features are the decoding targets, with the same number of rows as the dataset.

outer_crossval, tune_crossval, purge

Cross-validation, as in [banded_ridge_model()]: an integer fold count, a `cross_validation` object, or explicit folds; `tune_crossval` sets the inner folds used to choose the ridge penalty; `purge` drops training rows within that many rows of a held-out row.

alphas

Candidate ridge penalties. Each feature column selects its own penalty inside each outer-training set.

nuisance, nuisance_fit

Optional nuisance matrix (rows = observations) regressed out of patterns and targets inside every split, and how held-out rows are residualized; see [banded_ridge_model()].

partial

If `TRUE`, also report partial accuracies (see Metrics).

n_perm

Number of time-shift permutations; `0` (default) disables the null.

perm_strategy, perm_block, min_shift

Permutation scheme: `"circular_shift"` (default) or `"block_shuffle"`, the block length for the latter, and the smallest circular shift in rows.

min_voxels

Regions with fewer voxels are returned as errors.

seed

Integer seed for fold construction and permutations.

...

Passed to the model specification.

Value

A model specification of class `feature_decode_model`.

Details

The model shares its cross-validation, temporal purge, nuisance handling and ridge solvers with [banded_ridge_model()], with the roles of the two matrices exchanged. It implements [fit_roi()], so [run_searchlight()] and [run_regional()] work unchanged.

Metrics

One value per region or searchlight centre:

`all_r2`, `all_cor`

Mean held-out R2 and correlation over all feature columns.

`<set>_r2`, `<set>_cor`

The same, over the columns of one set or family. Every feature column counts equally.

`<contrast>_r2`, `<contrast>_cor`

Accuracy for the contrast series, i.e. observed and predicted features projected onto the contrast.

`<set>_partial_r2`, `<set>_partial_cor`

With `partial = TRUE`: accuracy for a set or family after every other feature column has been regressed out of both the pattern and the targets, with coefficients fitted on each training split. This is the pattern-level analogue of unique variance.

`<metric>_p`

With `n_perm > 0`: one-sided p-value against a null in which the predictions are shifted in time against the observations.

See also

[banded_ridge_model()], [feature_sets()], [run_searchlight()]

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n <- 80
ds <- gen_sample_dataset(c(5, 5, 5), nobs = n, blocks = 4)
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), n, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, c("m1", "p1", "ac")))
fs <- feature_sets(X, by_set(c("manner", "place", "acoustic")),
                   families = list(phonology = c("manner", "place")))
des <- feature_sets_design(fs, block_var_train = rep(1:4, each = 20),
                           time_series = TRUE)
model <- feature_decode_model(ds$dataset, des, outer_crossval = 4)
res <- run_searchlight(model, radius = 4, method = "standard")
